universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.notes: Research for this Minnesota expansion focused on DLI's own state-by-state reciprocity mechanism (see reciprocityRules); no separate Minnesota Universal License Recognition statute for electricians was independently identified. Absence of a finding is not evidence of absence — left Unknown rather than assumed false, matching the same caution applied in colorado-journeyman.json and arkansas-journeyman.json.

compactMembership.notes: Minnesota's mechanism issues a distinct 'personal license' to the applicant (Minnesota Statutes 326B.33, Subd. 20: 'The commissioner may issue a personal license...') via a state-by-state reciprocal agreement — not a single multistate license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact, e.g. the Nurse Licensure Compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating this reciprocal-agreement mechanism with a compact, matching the same reasoning already applied to Colorado's and Arkansas's reciprocity in their respective journeyman files.

reciprocityRules.value: Minnesota may issue a Class A Journeyworker (AJ) electrician license WITHOUT examination to applicants who obtained their journeyworker license by examination in one of 9 reciprocating states: Alaska, Arkansas, Colorado, Iowa, Montana, Nebraska, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming. To qualify, the applicant must hold the equivalent-class license from the reciprocating state in current good standing, have held it for at least one year, and have passed the license examination in that state (not obtained via a reciprocal agreement with a city or other political subdivision). The applicant must not have failed an examination for the same or greater license class in Minnesota, and if a prior Minnesota license expired more than two years ago, the exam must be retaken. A $50 application fee applies.

reciprocityRules.notes: Corroborated verbatim by the official reciprocity application form (form CC0502, directly read from the raw PDF: per-state class table lists 'Alaska (AJ only)... Arkansas (AJ only)... Colorado (AJ only)... Iowa (AM, AJ)... Montana (AJ only)... Nebraska (AM, AJ)... North Dakota (AM, AJ)... South Dakota (AM, AJ)... Wyoming (AJ only)' — see minnesota-dli-electrical-reciprocity-application) and by the exam-exemption statute itself, Minnesota Statutes 326B.33, Subdivision 20 (see minnesota-statute-326b-33). Unlike Arkansas, Minnesota's structure has no asymmetric tier-downgrade rule for the 4 states that also carry Master (AM) reciprocity — see minnesota-master.json for the separate, narrower Master-tier list and its own edge case.

endorsementRules.notes: Minnesota's own materials and statute describe this mechanism as 'reciprocity' specifically (Minn. Stat. 326B.33, Subd. 20 is titled 'Reciprocity') — no separate 'endorsement' pathway or terminology was identified, matching the same finding already recorded for Colorado and Arkansas.

requiredExams.value: No Minnesota examination is required for reciprocal Class A Journeyworker applicants: Minnesota Statutes 326B.33, Subdivision 20 explicitly authorizes the commissioner to 'issue a personal license without requiring the applicant to pass an examination' provided the applicant holds a valid comparable license from a state participating in the reciprocal agreement. This is a positively stated statutory exemption, not an inference. For ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) journeyworker licensure, a written exam ($50 exam fee) is required after accruing the necessary documented electrical work experience (Minnesota Rules 3800.3520, Subpart 1: 'As a precondition to issuance of any class of individual electrical license, an applicant is required to pass an examination').

requiredExperience.notes: For ORIGINAL (non-reciprocal) Minnesota journeyworker licensure — not the reciprocity pathway — an applicant must accrue documented electrical work experience before testing and meet a minimum age of 17 (per DLI's electrical licensing basics page); the exact hour schedule is set by Minnesota Rules 3800.3520, which was not independently quoted verbatim here. Recorded here in notes rather than the main value, to keep the reciprocity-relevant fact primary — matching the same pathway-distinguishing treatment already used in colorado-journeyman.json and arkansas-journeyman.json.

requiredEducation.notes: No standalone formal-education requirement distinct from the experience pathways already captured in requiredExperience was identified — matching the same scope decision already made in colorado-journeyman.json and arkansas-journeyman.json.

endorsementFeeUsd.notes: Minnesota's own reciprocity application fee (form CC0502) — the functional equivalent of this field's 'endorsement fee' concept, even though Minnesota's own terminology is 'reciprocity' not 'endorsement'. The same $50 amount applies to both Class A Journeyworker (AJ) and Class A Master (AM) reciprocal applications; a single combined form covers both classes. Not refundable per the form's own notice.
